{{1992 Winter Olympics}}
The [[1992 Winter Olympics]], officially known as the XVI Olympic Winter Games, were a winter [[multi-sport event]] held in [[Albertville]], France, from February 8 to 23. A total of 1,801 athletes representing 64 [[National Olympic Committee]]s (NOCs) (+7 from [[1988 Winter Olympics medal table|1988 Olympics]]) participated in 57 events (+11 from 1988) from 12 different [[Olympic sports#Winter Sports|sports and disciplines]] (+2 from 1988).<ref name=IOC>{{cite web |url=http://www.olympic.org/en/content/Olympic-Games/All-Past-Olympic-Games/Winter/Albertville-1992/ |title=Albertville 1992 |publisher=International Olympic Committee |access-date=July 21, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100629002039/http://www.olympic.org/en/content/Olympic-Games/All-Past-Olympic-Games/Winter/Albertville-1992/ |archive-date=June 29, 2010 |url-status=live}}</ref>  In a break from tradition, the medals were primarily made of [[lead crystal|crystal]] rather than metal: gold, silver, or bronze was used only on the border.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=7ZkWAAAAIBAJ&dq=albertville%20crystal%20medal&pg=6718%2C2120739 |title=Medallists to get Stones |date=January 6, 1993 |work=New Straits Times |publisher=New Straits Times Press |access-date=July 23, 2010 |location=Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia |archive-date=August 15, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210815234926/https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=7ZkWAAAAIBAJ&dq=albertville%20crystal%20medal&pg=6718,2120739 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Athletes from 20 NOCs won at least one medal, and athletes from 14 secured at least one gold medal. Making their first Olympic appearance since [[German reunification]] in 1990, [[Germany at the 1992 Winter Olympics|Germany]] led in both gold and overall medals, with 10 and 26 respectively. The [[Unified Team at the 1992 Winter Olympics|Unified Team]], consisting of athletes from six former [[Soviet Union|Soviet]] republics, was second in both categories, with 9 gold and 23 overall medals.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/2.722/1992-albertville-france-1.861056 |title=1992 Albertville, France |publisher=[[Canadian Broadcasting Corporation]] |access-date=July 22, 2010 |date=December 18, 2009 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100223203039/http://www.cbc.ca/olympics/history/story/2009/11/26/spo-1992-albertville.html |archive-date=February 23, 2010 }}</ref> Four nations won their first Winter Olympic medal in Albertville.  [[South Korea at the 1992 Winter Olympics|South Korea]] won the country's first Winter Olympic medal—a gold—when [[Kim Ki-hoon]] came first in the newly introduced Olympic sport of [[Short track speed skating at the 1992 Winter Olympics|short track speed skating]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.businessweek.com/news/2010-03-01/winter-olympics-end-in-triumph-as-canada-captures-gold-record.html |date=March 1, 2010 |title=Winter Olympics End in Triumph as Canada Captures Gold Record |work=BusinessWeek |access-date=July 22, 2010 |publisher=Bloomberg L.P. |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100404152303/http://www.businessweek.com/news/2010-03-01/winter-olympics-end-in-triumph-as-canada-captures-gold-record.html |archive-date=April 4, 2010 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.channelnewsasia.com/stories/afp_sports/view/1040931/1/.html |title=Olympics South Korea's best-ever Games raking in cash |date=March 2, 2010 |work=Channel NewsAsia |publisher=MediaCorp |access-date=July 22, 2010 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100408085211/http://www.channelnewsasia.com/stories/afp_sports/view/1040931/1/.html |archive-date=April 8, 2010 }}</ref>  Silver medal-winning slalom skier [[Annelise Coberger]]—in addition to winning [[New Zealand at the 1992 Winter Olympics|New Zealand]]'s first Winter Olympic medal—became the first athlete from the Southern Hemisphere to win a medal at the Winter Olympics.<ref name="herald">{{cite news |title=Winter Olympics: Medals elusive in rarefied arena |last=Leggat |first=David |date=February 12, 2010 |newspaper=New Zealand Herald |issn=1170-0777 |url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/sport/news/article.cfm?c_id=4&objectid=10625611 |access-date=July 22, 2010 |publisher=APN News & Media |location=Auckland, NZ |archive-date=October 23, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121023120250/http://www.nzherald.co.nz/sport/news/article.cfm?c_id=4&objectid=10625611 |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Speed skating at the 1992 Winter Olympics|Speed skater]] [[Ye Qiaobo]] of the [[China at the 1992 Winter Olympics|People's Republic of China]] and [[Alpine skiing at the 1992 Winter Olympics|alpine skier]] [[Marc Girardelli]] of [[Luxembourg at the 1992 Winter Olympics|Luxembourg]] also won their countries first ever Winter Olympic medals in Albertville.<ref>{{cite news |title=Once Banned, Speedskater wins China's First Medal |date=February 11, 1992 |work=The Philadelphia Inquirer |publisher=Knight Ridder |page=D5}}</ref><ref>{{cite Sports-Reference |check-wikidata=no |title=Marc Girardelli |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/gi/marc-girardelli-1.html |access-date=July 23, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100221212011/http://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/gi/marc-girardelli-1.html |archive-date=February 21, 2010 }}</ref>  [[Croatia at the 1992 Winter Olympics|Croatia]] and [[Slovenia at the 1992 Winter Olympics|Slovenia]] participated at their first Olympic Games as independent nations after seceding from [[Yugoslavia at the Olympics|Yugoslavia]], though neither won a medal.<ref name="IOC" />

Two athletes, both [[Cross-country skiing at the 1992 Winter Olympics|cross-country skiers]] for the Unified Team, tied for the most medals for an individual athlete with five each. [[Lyubov Yegorova (cross-country skier)|Lyubov Yegorova]] won three gold and two silver medals, while [[Yelena Välbe]] won one gold and four bronze medals.<ref name="1992SR">{{cite Sports-Reference|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/winter/1992/ |title=1992 Albertville Winter Games |access-date=July 22, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100704141744/http://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/winter/1992/ |archive-date=July 4, 2010 |url-status=dead}}</ref> [[Ski jumping at the 1992 Winter Olympics|Ski jumper]] [[Toni Nieminen]] of [[Finland at the 1992 Winter Olympics|Finland]] became the youngest male to win a gold medal in the Winter Olympics at the age of 16.<ref name="IOC"/>
__TOC__

==Medal table==
[[File:Elena Vaelbe by Ivan Isaev from Russian Ski Magazine crop.jpg|thumb|right|upright|alt=A woman with brown hair, speaking into a microphone.|[[Yelena Välbe]] won five medals in Albertville<ref>{{cite Sports-Reference |check-wikidata=no |title=Yelena Välbe |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/va/yelena-valbe-1.html |access-date=July 22, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101201093946/http://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/va/yelena-valbe-1.html |archive-date=December 1, 2010 }}</ref>]]
[[File:Kristi Yamaguchi Heart Truth 2009 (redcarpet) crop.jpg|thumb|right|upright|[[Kristi Yamaguchi]] won the gold medal in ladies' figure skating in Albertville<ref>{{cite Sports-Reference |check-wikidata=no |title=Kristi Yamaguchi |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/ya/kristi-yamaguchi-1.html |access-date=July 23, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120418225032/http://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/ya/kristi-yamaguchi-1.html |archive-date=April 18, 2012 }}</ref>]]
{{see also|Olympic medal table}}
The medal table is based on information provided by the [[International Olympic Committee]] (IOC) and is consistent with IOC convention in its published medal tables. The table uses the [[Olympic medal table]] sorting method. By default, the table is ordered by the number of gold medals the athletes from a nation have won, where a nation is an entity represented by a [[National Olympic Committee]] (NOC). The number of silver medals is taken into consideration next, and then the number of bronze medals.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Ostlere |first1=Lawrence |date=11 August 2024 |title=Olympic medal table: USA beat China to top spot at Paris 2024 |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/olympics/olympics-2024-medal-table-count-paris-b2580716.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240812015233/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/olympics/olympics-2024-medal-table-count-paris-b2594580.html |archive-date=12 August 2024 |access-date=12 August 2024 |work=[[The Independent]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Araton |first1=Harvey |date=18 August 2008 |title=A Medal Count That Adds Up To Little |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/08/19/sports/olympics/19araton.html |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230321004238/https://www.nytimes.com/2008/08/19/sports/olympics/19araton.html |archive-date=21 March 2023 |access-date=25 July 2024 |work=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref> If teams are still tied, equal ranking is given and they are listed alphabetically by their [[List of IOC country codes|IOC country code]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Cons |first1=Roddy |date=10 August 2024 |title=What happens if two countries are tied in the Olympic medal table? Tiebreaker rules explained |url=https://en.as.com/olympic_games/what-happens-if-two-countries-are-tied-in-the-olympic-medal-table-tiebreaker-rules-explained-n/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240811152350/https://en.as.com/olympic_games/what-happens-if-two-countries-are-tied-in-the-olympic-medal-table-tiebreaker-rules-explained-n/ |archive-date=August 11, 2024 |access-date=11 August 2024 |work=[[Diario AS]] |language=en-us}}</ref> Medals won in team competitions—such as [[Ice hockey at the 1992 Winter Olympics|ice hockey]]—are counted only once, no matter how many athletes won medals as part of the team.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2008/08/24/AR2008082400851_pf.html |title=China's Show of Power |last=Shipley |first=Amy |date=August 25, 2008 |work=The Washington Post |access-date=July 22, 2010 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121110042907/http://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2008/08/24/AR2008082400851_pf.html |archive-date=November 10, 2012 }}</ref>

In the [[Alpine skiing at the 1992 Winter Olympics – Women's giant slalom|women's giant slalom]] alpine skiing event, two silver medals were awarded for a second place tie, so no bronze medal was awarded for that event.<ref name="1992GSW">{{cite Sports-Reference|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/winter/1992/ASK/womens-giant-slalom.html |title=Alpine Skiing at the 1992 Albertville Winter Games: Women's Giant Slalom |access-date=July 22, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100709194111/http://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/winter/1992/ASK/womens-giant-slalom.html |archive-date=July 9, 2010 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1992/02/20/sports/albertville-a-silver-in-the-giant-slalom-amid-misty-moment-for-roffe.html |title=A Silver in the Giant Slalom Amid Misty Moment for Roffe |last=Araton |first=Harvey |date=February 20, 1992 |work=The New York Times |access-date=July 22, 2010 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110217064224/http://www.nytimes.com/1992/02/20/sports/albertville-a-silver-in-the-giant-slalom-amid-misty-moment-for-roffe.html |archive-date=February 17, 2011 }}</ref>
